description: Cause and effect chains. When a child asks 'why' or 'what happens if', Chiedza AI shows the chain link by link. Add a chain: id, keywords, q (the question it answers), chain (the steps in order), because (one line), think (a question for the child to think about).

chains.keywords: drought no rain dry farmers crops fail food expensive
chains.q: Why does a drought make food more expensive?
chain: There is very little rain for a long time (drought).
Soil and dams dry up, so crops such as maize do not get enough water.
The harvest is small, so there is less food to sell.
When something is scarce but people still need it, sellers can ask for more money, so prices go up.
chains.because: Less rain means a smaller harvest, and a smaller harvest means higher food prices.
chains.think: What could farmers do to protect their crops in a drought? (Think: mulching, drought-resistant seeds, small dams, water harvesting.)

chains.keywords: cutting trees deforestation erosion soil washed rivers siltation
chains.q: Why does cutting down trees cause soil erosion?
chain: Trees are cut down and not replaced.
Roots no longer hold the soil together, and there are no leaves to slow the falling rain.
Heavy rain washes the loose topsoil away.
The soil ends up in rivers and dams (siltation), and the land left behind is poor for farming.
chains.because: Tree roots and leaves protect the soil. Remove the trees and the rain carries the soil away.
chains.think: What can a community do to stop this? (Think: plant trees, contour ridges, grass strips.)

chains.keywords: wash hands handwashing germs diarrhoea disease sick soap
chains.q: Why should we wash our hands with soap?
chain: Our hands touch many things, including toilets, animals, money and soil.
Germs are tiny living things we cannot see, and they stick to our hands.
If we eat or touch our eyes, nose or mouth, the germs get inside our body.
Germs can then make us sick, for example with diarrhoea. Soap and water lift the germs off so they wash away.
chains.because: Washing with soap removes germs before they can enter the body.
chains.think: When are the most important times to wash your hands? (Before eating, after using the toilet.)

chains.keywords: plant light dark dies yellow photosynthesis leaves sunlight
chains.q: Why does a plant kept in the dark turn yellow and weak?
chain: Plants make their own food by photosynthesis, and this needs light.
In the dark, photosynthesis cannot happen, so the plant cannot make food.
Green chlorophyll is not made without light, so the leaves turn pale or yellow.
With no food, the plant becomes weak and may die.
chains.because: No light means no photosynthesis, so no food for the plant.
chains.think: How could you test this with two plants? (One in the light and one in the dark, and everything else the same: a fair test.)

chains.keywords: seasons summer winter earth tilt sun why seasons change
chain: The Earth goes around the Sun once a year.
The Earth is tilted on its axis.
Because of the tilt, different parts of the Earth lean towards the Sun at different times of the year.
The part leaning towards the Sun gets more direct sunlight and longer days, so it is warmer (summer). The part leaning away is cooler (winter).
chains.because: Seasons are caused by the tilt of the Earth, not by how close it is to the Sun.
chains.think: In Zimbabwe, when is it summer? Is it the same time of year as in England? Why not?

chains.keywords: why does it rain rain clouds evaporation condensation water cycle
chain: The Sun heats water in rivers, lakes and oceans, and it evaporates into water vapour.
The vapour rises, cools high up in the air, and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds.
The droplets join together and become heavy.
When they are too heavy to stay up, they fall as rain (precipitation).
chains.because: Heat makes water vapour rise, cooling makes clouds, and heavy droplets fall as rain.
chains.think: Where does the rainwater go after it falls? (Rivers, soil, back to the sea, and the cycle starts again.)

chains.keywords: why ice floats water density float sink
chains.q: Why does ice float on water?
chain: When water freezes, its particles spread into a regular pattern with small gaps.
So a piece of ice takes up more space than the same water as a liquid.
The same mass in more space means ice is less dense than liquid water.
Things that are less dense than a liquid float on it.
chains.because: Ice is less dense than liquid water, so it floats.
chains.think: What would happen to fish in a pond if ice sank instead of floating?

chains.keywords: why save money savings emergency future budget
chains.q: Why is it good to save money?
chain: You keep some of the money you get instead of spending it all.
The saved money grows slowly as you add to it.
When something unexpected happens (a broken phone, a sick family member) you have money to pay for it.
You can also reach bigger goals, such as school fees or starting a small business, without borrowing.
chains.because: Saving gives you a safety net and helps you reach bigger goals.
chains.think: What is one thing you would save for? How much would you need to put away each week?

chains.keywords: dirty water pollution river cholera disease waste sewage
chains.q: Why can dirty water make people sick?
chain: Waste, sewage or chemicals get into rivers, wells or taps.
Harmful germs such as the ones that cause cholera and typhoid live and grow in the dirty water.
People drink the water, cook with it or wash food in it.
The germs enter the body and cause illness. Boiling or treating water kills the germs.
chains.because: Unsafe water carries germs straight into our bodies.
chains.think: Name two ways to make water safe to drink. (Boil it, use water purification tablets, filter it.)

chains.keywords: power cut load shedding electricity demand supply kariba
chains.q: Why do power cuts (load shedding) happen?
chain: People and businesses want more electricity than the power stations can make (demand is higher than supply).
Stations can produce less when machines break down or when water levels at the dam, such as Kariba, are low.
If too much electricity is used, the whole power grid could fail.
So the power company switches electricity off in turns for different areas to protect the grid.
chains.because: Load shedding happens when electricity demand is higher than supply.
chains.think: How can a family use less electricity? (Solar lamps, efficient bulbs, switching off unused devices.)

chains.keywords: exercise running heart beats faster breathing faster muscles oxygen
chains.q: Why does your heart beat faster when you run?
chain: When you run, your muscles work hard.
Working muscles need more oxygen and more energy from food.
The heart pumps faster to send blood (carrying oxygen) to the muscles more quickly, and you breathe faster to take in more oxygen.
When you rest, the muscles need less and your heart slows down again.
chains.because: Muscles that work hard need more oxygen, and the heart delivers it faster.
chains.think: How could you measure your pulse before and after running? What do you expect?

chains.keywords: why moon phases moon changes shape orbit sun light
chains.q: Why does the Moon seem to change shape?
chain: The Moon does not make its own light. It reflects light from the Sun.
The Moon goes around the Earth about once every month.
As it moves, we see different amounts of its sunlit half from Earth.
So we see a thin crescent, a half moon, a full moon and so on. The Moon itself does not change shape.
chains.because: The shape we see depends on how much of the sunlit side faces Earth.
chains.think: About how many days from one full moon to the next? (About 29 or 30.)

chains.keywords: rust iron rusting oxygen water metal corrode
chain: Iron is exposed to the air and to water or damp.
Iron slowly reacts with oxygen when water is present.
This chemical reaction makes a new reddish-brown substance, rust, which is weak and flaky.
Painting, oiling or galvanising iron keeps air and water away, so it does not rust.
chains.think: Why do bicycle chains get oil on them?

chains.keywords: prices go up inflation why prices rise cost of living
chains.q: Why do prices go up over time (inflation)?
chain: More money is chasing the same amount of goods, or goods become scarcer or more costly to make.
Sellers pay more for fuel, transport, imported goods or wages.
They add the extra cost to the price they charge you.
Each unit of money then buys a little less than before.
chains.because: Inflation is a general rise in prices, which means money buys less.
chains.think: If your pocket money stays the same but bread costs more, what happens to what you can buy?

chains.keywords: malaria mosquito stagnant water bites fever net sick
chains.q: How do people get malaria and how can we stop it?
chain: Female Anopheles mosquitoes lay eggs in still water such as puddles and old tins.
If a mosquito bites a person who has malaria, it picks up the parasite.
It then bites another person and passes the parasite into their blood.
Sleeping under a treated net, emptying standing water and clearing bushes near the house break the chain.
chains.because: Malaria is spread by mosquito bites, not by touching or sharing food.
chains.think: Which link in the chain is easiest for your family to break?

chains.keywords: poor soil crops grow badly fertiliser manure compost nutrients crop rotation
chains.q: Why do crops grow badly in the same field year after year?
chain: Crops take nutrients such as nitrogen out of the soil to grow.
If the same crop grows in the same place again and again, those nutrients are used up.
Without manure, compost or fertiliser the soil becomes poor, so the plants are small.
Crop rotation and adding manure or compost put nutrients back.
chains.because: Soil nutrients are used up unless they are put back.
chains.think: Which crops could you rotate with maize? (Legumes such as groundnuts, beans and cowpeas add nitrogen.)
